To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
beta-lactam resistance in Gram-negative bacteria is a major problem in modern clinical microbiology and that the problem is likely to get worse.
beta-lactam antibiotic resistance is increasing in Gram-negative bacteria and that the resistance is due to new and old beta-lactam enzymes that have acquired new functions and properties.

the production of novel beta-lactam resistance determinants, such as the extended-spectrum beta-lactam-hydrolysing TEM and SHV enzymes and the metallo-beta-lactamase IMP-1, has been associated with outbreaks of nosocomial infections caused by Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in many hospitals worldwide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of antibiotic resistance in Gram-negative bacteria.
the development of new methods and technologies in the field of molecular biology, biotechnology and microbiology.
the study of the mechanisms by which bacteria acquire antibiotic resistance, with particular emphasis on resistance to beta-lactams, the most widely used antibiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Gram-negative bacteria are producing a greater number of beta-lactams with a wider variety of properties and that the number of Gram-negative bacteria producing multiple types of beta- lactamases has risen dramatically.

Gram-negative bacteria continue to evolve new beta-lactames with novel substrate profiles that are difficult to inhibit and that the production of multiple beta-lactam resistance mechanisms by the same pathogen is becoming more frequent.
beta-lactam resistance is a dynamic, evolving, and unpredictable process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new beta-lacatamases are the most serious threat to the continued clinical utility of beta-lactams.
we have found the new beta-lACTAMASES of gram-negative bacteria at the daw of the new millennium.
the evolution of the beta-lactams is a dynamic process that is still going on and will continue in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
beta-lactam resistance is not a static problem, and that beta-lactams should continue to be considered the cornerstone of antimicrobial therapy for Gram-negative bacterial infections.
the beta-lactams remain the most important class of antibiotics for the treatment of Gram-negative bacterial infections.
the production of novel beta-lactam enzymes is a dynamic process.
